prompt:
ONE image divided into 3 CLEAR PANELS of equal size, arranged left to right in a horizontal row, separated by generous clean cream gutters with NO drawn borders and NO frame lines. Each panel is one beat of the same argument and they read in order.

THE COLOUR RULE, and it governs everything: WARM AMBER GLOW MEANS SOUND. DEEP MUTED BRICK RED MEANS FAILED. A column is amber ONLY if it is whole from the bench all the way up. The instant a crack appears anywhere in a column, that pane AND EVERY PANE BELOW IT turn dull brick red, with NO amber remaining anywhere beneath the crack. There is never amber and red mixed in one column below a crack. The red is muted and earthy like old brick, never bright, never neon, never glowing.

THE FIGURE, the same person in all three panels and recognizably the same person in each: a woman in her mid-forties, South Asian, short dark hair going grey at the temples, wearing a plain olive canvas work apron over a grey long-sleeved shirt.

THE SETTING, one consistent world across all three panels: a warm workshop at dusk with a wooden bench. Tall columns of stacked translucent panes rise up out of an open laptop on the bench and continue past the top edge of the panel, so the layers live INSIDE the laptop while she works in the warm real room OUTSIDE it.

BEAT ONE: ONE column. A jagged brick red crack has torn a pane HIGH up, near the top of the panel. That pane and EVERY pane below it, all the way down to the laptop, are dull brick red. There is NO amber anywhere in this column. In her hands is a finished piece, also dull red and split. She is looking up at the high crack, understanding where it came from.

BEAT TWO: The SAME red column. She is bent over the lowest panes with hand tools, actively trying to mend them, brow furrowed, working hard. The panes she is touching remain stubbornly dull red. Her repair is changing nothing and the whole column above her stays red. NO amber appears anywhere in this panel.

BEAT THREE: She has set her tools down and TURNED AWAY from the red column, which is now at the far edge of the frame, still red. She stands before a DIFFERENT column, whole and unbroken, glowing warm sound amber from the bench all the way up past the top edge of the panel, with no crack anywhere in it. In her hands is a finished piece that is whole and glowing amber. She is calm and satisfied. This is a choice, not a repair.

TEXT FURNITURE, in the cream margins only and never over the artwork. Reproduce every string character-exact and add no other lettering anywhere:
Title bar, centered in the cream margin ABOVE the panels, in caps: THE ALIGNMENT STACK
Caption in the cream gutter UNDER panel one, in caps: A CRACK ABOVE RUINS BELOW
Caption in the cream gutter UNDER panel two, in caps: YOU CANNOT PATCH IT HERE
Caption in the cream gutter UNDER panel three, in caps: CHOOSE A SOUND STACK
Footer bar, centered in the cream margin BELOW the panels, in caps: SELECT YOUR UPSTREAM, DO NOT REPAIR IT

Any other writable surface in frame is BLANK: no labels on the panes, no writing on the bench, no text on the laptop screen, no numbers anywhere.

ABSOLUTELY NOT: a denim jacket, a jean jacket, any chest patch, any smiley-face badge, any enamel pin, any embroidered emblem, a white tee under an open jacket. No recurring branded character and no identifiable real individual. No neon, no 3D or CGI rendering, no glossy plastic, no HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, no power armor.

warm editorial illustration, soft painterly line and gentle shading, muted natural palette on a warm cream ground, grounded and human, picture-book register for adults

Do NOT render it in any of these styles: comic-book, cartoon mascot, flat vector, neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, photoreal, anime, any identifiable recurring individual's face or signature clothing.
